question: Should Crabbox accept ordered `!` negation with `\!` as the compatibility contract for `.crabboxignore` and `sync.exclude`?
rationale: The implementation is now coherent and proven, but it intentionally changes the meaning of existing unescaped leading-bang exclude strings, which is an upgrade compatibility decision automation cannot own.

options.title: Accept the documented escape contract
options.body: Merge after normal checks if maintainers are comfortable reserving unescaped `!` for negation and requiring `\!` for literal paths.

options.title: Preserve literal bang compatibility
options.body: Ask for a redesign or opt-in syntax if existing unescaped leading-bang excludes must keep their old meaning by default.

options.title: Defer the matcher expansion
options.body: Pause or close this PR if Crabbox should not expand exclude semantics in core right now.

recommendation.title: Accept the documented escape contract
recommendation.body: Merge after normal checks if maintainers are comfortable reserving unescaped `!` for negation and requiring `\!` for literal paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the recent sync matcher history and pushed the current fixup that defines the compatibility contract under review.
